main_text.l: Oro autem aeternum & omnipotente Dei Patris filium, imaginem eius & Characte-rem personae illius, Dominum nostrũ Iesum Christum, vt pro infinita sua erga nos fratres & coharedes suos beneuolentia nos totos sanctificet, & in nostris & aliorum pio-rum cordibus accendat, foueat & conseruet lucem verae doctrinae, fiduciam nostrae cum Deo consociationis & coniunctionis, charitatem denique erga fidei nostrae consortes, alienâ ab omni hypocrysi & fuco: ad laudem sanc-ti nominis sui, & omnium nostrum salu-tem. Dixi.
Reuocauit mihi, Magnifice Domine Rector, Generosi & clarissimi viri, Candidatus noster ornatissimus, in memoriam elegàs inprimis Prouerbium: πόλις ἀνδρὰ διδάσκει[?]: Respublica virum docet.

Quemadmodum enim egregio suo merito Politici gubernatores, omne punctum ferunt, qui Themistocli similes sunt, de quo Thucydid. ait: ἡρξατο[?] γὰρ[?] ἀλλ'[?] οὕτω[?] αὐτοχεδιάσας[?] τὰ δὲ ἄλλα ἐγένετο[?]: ita etiam Theologi egregiâ meretur laudem, quando de rebus magnis

page.notes: Long s is read as s throughout. Line-end hyphens "Characte-rem", "pio-rum", "sanc-ti", "salu-tem" are kept as printed. The Greek of the Thucydides quotation is only partly legible at this scan resolution; the marked words are best readings and need checking against the edition. The Greek in the Proverb line is also uncertain in its final word. "Candidatus" was read from a worn letter. The tilde in "nostrũ" is kept as printed. Show-through from the facing page appears faintly in the left margin and is not transcribed. The bottom catchword "inter-" is the start of the next line on the following page.
